key_insight: This paper shows that unsupervised domain adaptation can help mammography models stay accurate when they are tested on data from hospitals or sites they have never seen before. The approach improves benign vs. malignant calcification classification by reducing the performance drop caused by multi-site dataset shifts.
problem_solved: It addresses the domain shift problem in mammography CAD systems, where models trained on one site often perform poorly on unseen sites due to differences in scanners, imaging protocols, and patient populations.
method: Builds a calcification classification framework for benign vs. malignant breast disease in multi-site mammography data.
Uses unsupervised domain adaptation to transfer knowledge from labeled source sites to unlabeled target sites.
Aims to learn domain-invariant features so the classifier generalizes better across institutions.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work highlights a practical path toward more robust medical imaging models that generalize beyond a single dataset. It is especially relevant for deploying AI in real clinical settings where cross-site variability is unavoidable.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing source-site training and target-site adaptation

paper_title: Unsupervised Domain Adaptation for Calcification Classification in Mammography Across Multi-Site Datasets
paper_authors: Xuan Liu, Derek L. Nguyen, Emily C. Barre, Jennifer Thomas, Thomas Lynch
